### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | AI tools may be used for writing assistance, data analysis, or generating images, but disclosure is mandatory: tool name/version, dates and access info, and a full description of use (acknowledgments/footnote for text, methods section for data analysis, figure captions for images). AI cannot be listed as an author (cannot meet accountability requirements). Minor uses (spelling/language check, single words/brief phrases, minor formatting) are exempt from declaration. This is BBS's own author-instructions page but its language overlaps heavily with Cambridge University Press's generic Research Publishing Ethics Guidelines (Cambridge was first major publisher to set AI ethics policy, March 2023) -- treat as journal-adopted-generic rather than BBS-bespoke. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/behavioral-and-brain-sciences/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Cross-disciplinary theoretical/synthesis pieces in psychology, neuroscience, behavioral biology, and cognitive science judged 'particularly significant and controversial' enough to sustain 10-30 open commentaries. The most recent target article on Cambridge Core's latest-issue page (Vol 49, 2026) is Manvir Singh's 'Goals, power, and selection: Foundational issues in the naturalistic study of culture,' with commentaries spanning cultural convergence, language/symbol evolution, institutions and inequality, moral progress, and cognitive/emotional bases of culture -- indicating current welcome for large-scope theoretical/synthetic treatments of cultural evolution and social cognition, not narrow empirical reports (single-issue snapshot, not a trend claim).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** theoretical/synthesis articles that formally model or systematize a body of research, novel interpretation or critique of existing experimental/theoretical work, empirical research explicitly framed for broad interdisciplinary implications (not narrow specialty findings), cultural evolution and social-cognition theorizing (current-issue emphasis, single-issue snapshot only)

### Framing Requirements

- **Framing requirement noted by AI research:** Per official target-article criteria: submission must be either (i) empirical research framed as having broader interdisciplinary scope/implications than a specialty journal would carry, (ii) a formally modeled/systematized theoretical article of unusual significance, or (iii) a novel interpretation/synthesis/critique of existing experimental or theoretical work. Chinese-language sources (LetPub, tangential Zhihu results) independently describe the bar as very high rejection difficulty and note target articles rarely have Chinese first/corresponding authors -- unverified anecdotal observation, not documented policy.
